raw_text:
{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "fametrano",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "concerned tests lack nonce and BIP324 key isolation checks"
    },
    {
      "login": "vasild",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "finds reliance on DNS seeds and excluding Tor/I2P peers unacceptable"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:6397196009",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Tests do not verify that attempts use unique nonces and BIP324 keys, allowing regressions that let recipients link broadcasts to pass undetected.",
      "quote": "This PR's tests do not check that each attempt gets its own VERSION nonce, PING nonce and BIP324 key (A4 in `doc/design/private-broadcast.md`), so a regression there would pass.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author initially deferred but edited reply stating they changed their mind and brought it forward",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6405247174"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6405247174",
      "status_by_quote": "changed my mind and brought it forward"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Relying permanently on centralized DNS seeds for each private broadcast creates a single point of failure and makes the feature vulnerable to outages or censorship.",
      "quote": "I do not think that it is reasonable to start relying on a few servers permanently (not just once in a lifetime, but every time a node wants to privately broadcast a transaction).",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied explaining seed downtime only stops broadcasts without leaking identity, whereas addrman introduces sybil leaks",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6424580079"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "If the seeds go offline, private broadcast stops; it doesn't leak."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Broadcasting exclusively to IP peers via Tor makes private broadcast fragile to Tor outages and exit node failures, lacking an I2P fallback.",
      "quote": "Only broadcasting to IP peers via the Tor network would make the feature too fragile - it would rely on the Tor network and the Tor exit nodes working properly.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that Tor privacy outweighs its centralization and gathering addresses without seeder nodes reintroduces leaks",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6424580079"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "Tor isn't decentralized either, but we accept utility in terms of privacy."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Restricting broadcast recipients to IP peers degrades network-wide privacy by preventing Tor and I2P nodes from acting as indistinguishable recipients.",
      "quote": "Even moderate adoption of private broadcast in its current form improves the privacy of everybody because everybody could be a recipient. ... That would be spoiled if we only send to IP peers.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that master's recipient model allows easy sybiling leading to IP leaks and offers limited attack resistance",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6424580079"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "The attacks it resists are quite limited today, and therefore it's sort of in purgatory where we can't make any promises about it."
    }
  ],
  "support": [],
  "notes": "vasild raised fundamental architectural objections against relying on DNS seeds and excluding Tor/I2P peers as private broadcast destinations. instagibbs answered each point defending the privacy rationale. instagibbs also edited his earlier reply to fametrano indicating he brought forward the requested test checks.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "vasild to evaluate author's response on DNS seeds and Tor/I2P peer handling",
      "id": "c:6424580079"
    },
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "fametrano to follow up after author brought forward test checks",
      "id": "c:6405247174"
    }
  ]
}

participants.note: concerned tests lack nonce and BIP324 key isolation checks
finds reliance on DNS seeds and excluding Tor/I2P peers unacceptable

claims.text: Tests do not verify that attempts use unique nonces and BIP324 keys, allowing regressions that let recipients link broadcasts to pass undetected.
claims.quote: This PR's tests do not check that each attempt gets its own VERSION nonce, PING nonce and BIP324 key (A4 in `doc/design/private-broadcast.md`), so a regression there would pass.
claims.status_note: author initially deferred but edited reply stating they changed their mind and brought it forward
claims.status_by_quote: changed my mind and brought it forward

claims.text: Relying permanently on centralized DNS seeds for each private broadcast creates a single point of failure and makes the feature vulnerable to outages or censorship.
claims.quote: I do not think that it is reasonable to start relying on a few servers permanently (not just once in a lifetime, but every time a node wants to privately broadcast a transaction).
claims.status_note: author replied explaining seed downtime only stops broadcasts without leaking identity, whereas addrman introduces sybil leaks
claims.status_by_quote: If the seeds go offline, private broadcast stops; it doesn't leak.

claims.text: Broadcasting exclusively to IP peers via Tor makes private broadcast fragile to Tor outages and exit node failures, lacking an I2P fallback.
claims.quote: Only broadcasting to IP peers via the Tor network would make the feature too fragile - it would rely on the Tor network and the Tor exit nodes working properly.
claims.status_note: author replied that Tor privacy outweighs its centralization and gathering addresses without seeder nodes reintroduces leaks
claims.status_by_quote: Tor isn't decentralized either, but we accept utility in terms of privacy.

claims.text: Restricting broadcast recipients to IP peers degrades network-wide privacy by preventing Tor and I2P nodes from acting as indistinguishable recipients.
claims.quote: Even moderate adoption of private broadcast in its current form improves the privacy of everybody because everybody could be a recipient. ... That would be spoiled if we only send to IP peers.
claims.status_note: author replied that master's recipient model allows easy sybiling leading to IP leaks and offers limited attack resistance
claims.status_by_quote: The attacks it resists are quite limited today, and therefore it's sort of in purgatory where we can't make any promises about it.

result.notes: vasild raised fundamental architectural objections against relying on DNS seeds and excluding Tor/I2P peers as private broadcast destinations. instagibbs answered each point defending the privacy rationale. instagibbs also edited his earlier reply to fametrano indicating he brought forward the requested test checks.
